Houses.traditional_name: House of the Querent (Helm / House of Self)
Houses.astrological_correspondence: Life, Body, and the Querent's Person
governs: The querent's life, vitality, and physical body
Complexion, stature, bearing, and general constitution
Name and outward character as brought to this question
The querent's vehicle when framed as their conveyance
Immediate local weather or conditions at the querent's location
The seat from which the whole shield is read when no third party is named
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: Practically never. The First is the querent's seat. Only in dedicated life-reading questions does it double as the quesited.
Houses.notes: Mercury rejoices in the helm. Read the First before assigning any house to the quesited: every other testimony is measured against the querent's condition, bearing, and capacity to act.
Houses.interpretive_essence: The querent as they sit in the matter: body, vitality, bearing, and the condition brought to the question.
read_when: Always read first, before any other house
When establishing the querent's figure before assigning a house to the quesited
When testing agreement or conflict between the querent and the house of the matter
When the question names no distinct other party
When judging the querent's capacity to act, apart from the outcome shown elsewhere
common_misreadings: Treating the First as modern identity psychology rather than concrete body, vitality, and bearing
Placing a spouse, rival, or partner here instead of the Seventh
Reading the First as fixed personality typing rather than the condition brought to this question
Houses.classical_note: The First is the seat the querent occupies. Every other house is read in relation to it.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: When the First shows a passive multitude while ally houses flare, ask whether the narrative is curated for witnesses before you trust surface testimony.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Money, Movable Goods, and the Querent's Substance
governs: The querent's own money, income, and financial condition
Movable goods and personal possessions
Profit, gain, and loss in the querent's own dealings
The querent's credit: capacity to raise, borrow, or repay
Theft or loss of the querent's belongings, and their recovery
Concrete material sustenance, not abstract self-worth
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns the querent's own money, goods in hand, pay, personal theft, or solvency.
Houses.notes: Liquidity lives here: what moves across the table. Land and titles belong to the Fourth; venture and wager to the Fifth; another person's substance to the Eighth.
example_questions: Will my business make or lose money?
Will the investment be profitable?
Will I get paid for the work I did?
Is this a good time to borrow money?
Is the antique table worth what the seller is asking?
Will the package I shipped arrive safely?
Has my missing watch been stolen?
Will my stolen car be recovered?
Houses.interpretive_essence: The querent's own means: cash, income, movable goods, pay, and the fate of belongings lost or stolen.
read_when: When the question concerns the querent's own cash, pay, income, or net worth
When judging whether the querent can afford, raise, or repay a sum
When the querent's goods have gone missing or been stolen
When weighing the material cost of a decision against the court's verdict
common_misreadings: Using the Second for a partner's or opponent's income, which belongs to the Eighth
Routing real estate or land value through the Second instead of the Fourth
Treating value as modern self-worth psychology rather than literal cash and goods
Houses.classical_note: The Second is always the querent's own substance. Another party's purse is the Eighth.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Amissio on the Second with Acquisitio in the Fifth can show money moving through risk and back. Follow the sequence of houses, not one figure alone.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Near Kin, Messages, and Short Journeys
governs: Siblings, cousins, and near kin
Neighbors and immediate community relations
Short or local journeys, traditionally within about a day's range
Letters, messages, rumor, and news
Elementary schooling and basic skill-learning
Everyday, low-formality communication
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns a sibling or cousin, a neighbor, a short journey, or the reliability of a message or rumor.
Houses.notes: The Moon rejoices among letters, cousins, and short wheels. Discern signal from noise before you build strategy on chatter.
example_questions: Will my relationship with my sister improve?
Will the neighbors agree to an easement?
Is this a good weekend to drive to the beach?
Should I enroll my child in North Central Elementary?
Is my neighbor George's advice worth following?
Is the news story accurate?
Should I believe the rumors?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Near kin, neighbors, short journeys, letters, rumor, and the local news that feeds or unsettles a decision.
read_when: When the question names a sibling, cousin, or neighbor rather than a parent or spouse
When judging a short trip, errand, or local journey
When testing whether a rumor, letter, or piece of news is reliable
When distinguishing a near or local matter from the Ninth's far travel or doctrine
common_misreadings: Assigning modern communication psychology to the Third rather than concrete letters, kin, and errands
Calling a long or foreign journey Third when it belongs to the Ninth
Confusing a parent with a sibling here
Houses.classical_note: The Third carries near kin and near travel. Doctrinal, ancestral, or long-range matters belong to the Ninth.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Conjunctio in the Third with Carcer in the Ninth can show local talk running free while paperwork stays blocked upstream.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Land, Father, and the End of the Matter
governs: The querent's father and paternal lineage
Land, houses, real property, and buildings
Agriculture, soil, and buried or hidden things
The end or final state of any matter
Old age and the close of life's arc
Cities and settled places in mundane usage
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns land or a house, the father, agriculture, buried or hidden objects, or explicitly asks how a matter will end.
Houses.notes: Angular earth: foundations, closure, and the voice that pronounces how a matter lands when dust settles. Many lineages let the Fourth speak last when other houses have argued their parts.
example_questions: Is the property worth buying?
Is the soil fertile?
Will roses flourish here?
Should I move to another apartment?
Is Springfield a good place to relocate?
Is the table antique or a modern reproduction?
Is the pension fund in reliable hands?
How is my father doing?
How will the present situation turn out in the end?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Land, home, the father line, ancestry, and the final outcome when the question asks how a matter ends.
read_when: When the question explicitly asks how a matter will finally turn out
When land, a house, or real property is the literal subject
When the father, patrimony, or ancestral matters are named
When something must be verified as buried, hidden underground, or foundational
common_misreadings: Using the Fourth for the mother when the working tradition assigns her to the Tenth
Treating any dark topic as Fourth rather than checking the Eighth or Twelfth
Skipping the completion read when the question explicitly asks how something ends
Houses.classical_note: The Fourth closes the wheel: land, the father, and the end of the matter. Do not reach for it merely because a topic feels grave.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Fortuna Major in the Fourth with Via in the Tenth can show domestic stability underwriting a public pivot. Weigh which angular message bears more literal weight.

governs: Children and pregnancy
Pleasure, banquets, entertainment, and courtship's sensual side
Gambling, speculation, and games of chance
Messengers and go-betweens acting on another's behalf
Taverns and places of festivity
Fertility of crops in agricultural questions
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns children, pregnancy, gambling or speculation, an embassy or go-between, or pleasure not bound by contract.
Houses.notes: Venus rejoices where joy is cultivated. The bond between two people belongs to the First and Seventh axis, not to a hard split between casual and serious romance.
example_questions: Will the grape crop be good this year?
Is Janis interested in me sexually?
Is my unborn child a boy or a girl?
How well will my four-year-old cope with a baby brother?
Will the concert be worth the ticket price?
Is next Friday a good night for the party?
Is the new Asian restaurant in town worth a visit?
Will the dress be ready in time for the wedding?
How will fishing be on the lake this weekend?
Will it rain tomorrow?
Will I receive a letter from my grandmother?
Are the claims in the book I'm reading accurate?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Pleasure and what it produces: children, entertainment, creative risk, and the honest wager.
read_when: When the question concerns conception, pregnancy, or a child's welfare
When judging a wager, speculative venture, or game of chance
When the matter is pleasure, festivity, or courtship rather than a committed bond
When a go-between or messenger's mission is the actual subject
common_misreadings: Making the Fifth the default romance house while ignoring the Seventh's role in reciprocal bonds
Folding all creative work here without checking whether the trade is Sixth labor or Tenth vocation
Reading sexuality here as identical to modern Eighth-house intimacy
Houses.classical_note: The Fifth governs pleasure and its issue, including children and speculation. Bonds between people belong to the First and Seventh.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Puella in the Fifth with Rubeus in the Eighth can tie pleasure to another party's obligation. Read both houses before isolating romance.

governs: Sickness, disease, and bodily affliction
Servants, employees, and those laboring under the querent's direction
Small livestock and household animals
Hired trades and service work performed for another
Daily labor, toil, and routine upkeep
Practitioners of occult arts other than the querent, when hired as service
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns an illness, a servant or employee, a small domestic animal, or hired labor.
Houses.notes: Mars rejoices in labor, small animals, and the body's daily ledger. Illness here is disruption of rhythm and capacity. Death and the other party's resources belong to the Eighth.
example_questions: Should I hire Phyllis?
Are my employees stealing from the till?
Are the plumbers reliable?
Should I hire a band for the party?
Will I find my lost dog?
Will hogs fetch a good price this fall?
How serious is this illness?
Would it be worthwhile to get a Tarot reading from Marie?
Is this a good time to have dental work done?
Will I catch the flu this winter?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Sickness and regimen, hired help, service trades, pets, and the daily work that keeps life runnable.
read_when: When the question is specifically about an illness, its course, or severity
When judging the loyalty, competence, or fitness of an employee or servant
When a pet or small domestic animal is the named subject
When distinguishing day-labor and service from the vocation and honor of the Tenth
common_misreadings: Sorting occupations into Sixth or Tenth by prestige rather than by service versus office
Sending every case of exhaustion to the Twelfth instead of examining Sixth workload
Reading modern wellness psychology into the Sixth rather than concrete illness
Houses.classical_note: The Sixth judges sickness and service. Title, promotion, and public role belong to the Tenth.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Carcer in the Sixth with Laetitia in the Twelfth can show grinding duty relieved by private respite. Check boundaries and recovery.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: The Other Party, Contracts, and Open Conflict
governs: The querent's spouse or committed partner
Open enemies, litigants, and adversaries in dispute
Contracts and agreements made face to face between two parties
Thieves as persons, distinct from the theft itself
Runaways and fugitives when the question is whether they will be found
In dedicated medical charts, the physician
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns a spouse or partner, a business counterpart, an open adversary or lawsuit, or the identity of a thief.
Houses.notes: The descendant angle faces the other: lover, opponent, or signatory across the table. To read that person's own resources or condition in depth, turn the chart from the Seventh.
example_questions: Does Stanley love me?
Will this relationship last?
Is this a good time to propose marriage?
Should Carol and I form a business partnership?
Should I sign the contract?
Will the Packers win the Super Bowl?
Will India and Pakistan sign a peace treaty?
Will my company's bid on the project be accepted?
Would it be to my advantage to file a lawsuit?
Will the police catch the thief?
Is next weekend a good time for deer hunting?
Will I be able to get in contact with Julie again?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Whoever stands opposite the querent: partner, counterpart, litigant, competitor, or thief.
read_when: When a specific other person stands opposite the querent in the matter
When the question is whether to enter, keep, or dissolve a mutual agreement
When a thief must be characterized or located
When turning the chart to read the other party's concerns from a derived First house
common_misreadings: Restricting the Seventh to romance alone and missing lawsuits, rivals, and thieves
Placing the other party's money in the Seventh instead of the Eighth
Forcing someone into the Seventh before a genuine reciprocal tie exists in the question
Houses.classical_note: The Seventh is whoever meets the querent face to face, in love or in conflict. Turn the chart for that person's own particulars.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Puer in the Seventh with Albus in the First can pit a sharp rival against a softly spoken querent. Precision of terms matters more than volume.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Death, Inheritance, and the Other's Substance
governs: Death and matters directly contiguous with it
Inheritance, legacies, and dowry or portion
The resources or support of the person shown in the Seventh
Money lent out by the querent, once it sits in another's hands
Fear and dread as a classical topic
Absence and missing persons in traditional usage
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns death or its immediate aftermath, inheritance or dowry, or whether another named party will provide support or repay a debt.
Houses.notes: Classical geomancy treats the Eighth as the Second from the Seventh. Spiritual seeking is Ninth; secrecy and occult harm against the querent lean Twelfth; ancestry and the grave lean Fourth.
example_questions: Will he support me financially?
Should I get life insurance?
How seriously should I take Bill's threats?
Is this a good time to make a will?
Will I receive the inheritance I was promised?
Is my neighbor's missing daughter all right?
Will I ever get back the book I loaned to Greg?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Death, absence, loans out, inheritance, and the resources of whoever stands in the Seventh.
read_when: When the question concerns death or matters following directly from a death
When judging whether another named party will support the querent materially
When a debt or loan already given out must be traced or recovered
When inheritance, dowry, or a legacy is explicitly the subject
key_significators: The other party's money and means
common_misreadings: Reading the Eighth as intimacy or psychological transformation through modern Scorpio association
Placing hidden enemies or secrecy here rather than in the Twelfth
Confusing death with ancestry, burial, or afterlife, which lean Fourth and Ninth
Houses.classical_note: The Eighth is the Second from the Seventh: death and the other party's substance, not sex, secrecy, or spirituality.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Cauda in the Eighth with Caput in the Second can mark closure of a debt opening a new cash chapter. Honor order of events.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Far Travel, Faith, and Higher Learning
governs: Long journeys, voyages, and travel to distant or foreign places
Religion, clergy, and matters of faith or doctrine
Dreams and visions when their meaning is under inquiry
Higher education, universities, and advanced formal study
Law as a body of learning and legal philosophy
Publishing, astrology, and divination as disciplines
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns long-distance travel, religion or faith, formal higher study, or the interpretation of a dream.
Houses.notes: The Sun rejoices on long roads, in print, and in faith argued under open sky. Litigation itself stays in the Seventh even when law as a discipline is Ninth.
example_questions: Will I be able to go to Germany this summer?
How congested will the airport be?
Should I pursue my interest in Pagan religion?
Will I be able to get into Harvard?
Is this a good time to go back to school and finish my degree?
Should I sign up for music lessons, or would I be wasting my time?
Does the dream I had last night mean anything?
Should I study geomancy?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Far travel, religion, higher study, dreams under inquiry, and divinatory doctrine as a discipline.
read_when: When a journey is long-distance, overseas, or beyond the Third's local range
When the question concerns faith, religious vocation, or doctrine
When a dream's meaning, rather than its cause alone, is under inquiry
When judging entry into or progress through university-level study
common_misreadings: Treating occult topics as automatically Eighth because they feel uncanny, when seeking belongs here
Calling a routine commute Ninth rather than Third
Conflating law as discipline with an active lawsuit in the Seventh
Houses.classical_note: The Ninth carries the far horizon: distant travel, doctrine, and higher learning. Hidden harm belongs to the Twelfth.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Via in the Ninth with Populus in the Third can show distant plans running ahead of local facts. Verify channels before you advise.

governs: Career, profession, and public vocation
Honor, reputation, and public standing
Kings, magistrates, employers, and those in authority over the querent
The querent's mother, per Lilly's classical convention
Public offices, governments, and matters of rule
Prescribed treatment in dedicated medical charts
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns career, promotion or dismissal, an authority figure or employer, public honor, or the mother under the tradition being followed.
Houses.notes: Midheaven angle: headline name, boss or crown, collective weather. Day-to-day labor under the same employer remains the Sixth's domain.
example_questions: Should I look for a different job?
Will I get the promotion?
Will I get along with my new boss?
Will the county office approve my building permit?
How is Mom doing these days?
Will Senator Smith win reelection?
Should I run for a seat on the school board?
Will the weather tomorrow be clear and dry?
Should I get a second opinion on the proposed treatment for my heart condition?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Public office, career, reputation, authority figures, and collective weather. In Lilly's convention the mother is read here as well.
read_when: When career advancement, dismissal, or professional standing is the named subject
When an authority figure, employer, or governing body must be judged
When the querent's mother is the subject under the tradition being followed
When public reputation or honor, rather than private character, is at stake
common_misreadings: Sorting jobs into Sixth versus Tenth by prestige rather than by service versus standing
Assuming the mother is always Fourth when the classical horary line runs Tenth
Collapsing personal identity in the First into professional identity here
Houses.classical_note: The Tenth carries office and honor. Day-to-day labor and hired service remain the Sixth's domain.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Fortuna Minor in the Tenth with Tristitia in the Fourth can show visible success stressing domestic foundations.

governs: Friends, allies, and well-wishers
Hope, trust, and expectation of good
Benefactors, patrons, and unearned favor
Counselors and advisors acting in the querent's interest
Annual crops in agricultural questions
Questions the querent declines to state aloud
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns a friend, benefactor, or ally, matters of hope and trust, or an unearned gift or favor.
Houses.notes: Jupiter rejoices among friends, benefactors, and the crop that closes the season. Once a formal bond is named, move to the Seventh.
example_questions: How is my old college buddy Bill doing?
Will my friend Sally make good on her promise?
Can I count on the neighborhood association to support me?
Will I achieve my fondest dream?
Will I get a good crop of peas this year?
I don't want to tell you what my question is; can you answer it anyway?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Friends, allies, patrons, hope, and questions the querent will not name aloud.
read_when: When a friend, ally, or benefactor's reliability or intent is the subject
When the question turns on hope or expectation rather than an enforceable agreement
When a gift or favor given without formal contract is at issue
When the querent withholds the true question and general goodwill must be assessed
common_misreadings: Treating any online contact as automatically Eleventh without asking its real function
Promising a favorable outcome from hopeful testimony alone
Confusing a patron's goodwill with a contractual partner in the Seventh
Houses.classical_note: The Eleventh governs friends and hope freely given. Formal bonds belong to the Seventh.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Rubeus in the Eleventh with Populus in the First can show a volatile circle cheering a querent who remains inwardly undecided.

Houses.astrological_correspondence: Hidden Enemies, Confinement, and Large Beasts
governs: Hidden or unrecognized enemies
Imprisonment, confinement, exile, or institutional restraint
Large or working animals: horses, oxen, cattle, beasts of burden
Sorrow and self-undoing whose source is not yet visible
Witchcraft or malicious craft worked against the querent by another
Treachery and betrayal not yet uncovered
Houses.significator_of_quesited_when: The question concerns an unidentified or hidden enemy, imprisonment or confinement, a large working animal, or suspected malice against the querent.
Houses.notes: Saturn rejoices in what stays unseen. Spiritual seeking belongs to the Ninth. Secrecy and hidden enmity are Twelfth, not Eighth.
example_questions: Will I be able to pay my bills next month?
Will I be sent to prison?
Is Ruth hiding something from me?
Is someone at work trying to get me fired?
Was the poppet in the front yard a joke, or is someone trying to cast a spell on me?
Is this horse worth buying?
Will cattle fetch a good price this year?
Houses.interpretive_essence: Hidden enemies, confinement, large livestock, and historically malicious magic cast against the querent.
read_when: When an enemy or threat is suspected but not yet identified or named
When confinement, imprisonment, or institutional restriction is the literal subject
When a large working animal is the named subject
When the querent suspects hidden malice, sabotage, or witchcraft directed against them
common_misreadings: Softening the Twelfth into modern spirituality rather than concrete hidden threat and confinement
Naming a secret enemy from Twelfth testimony alone, without corroboration elsewhere
Confusing self-inflicted sorrow here with illness and regimen in the Sixth
Houses.classical_note: The Twelfth holds what works against the querent unseen. Spiritual seeking reads through the Ninth, and death through the Eighth.
Houses.figure_combinations_to_watch: Laetitia in the Twelfth with Carcer in the Sixth can show relief inside constraint, such as humane ward or structured care.
